observations.text: Climate science establishes a problem frame; mitigation, circular economy, and food systems examine different places where responses can act. Their combination keeps sustainability from shrinking into a list of individual habits. It connects environmental processes with choices about energy, materials, and the organization of production.

Circular design and material choices make the economic idea more concrete. Renewable energy and storage provide a parallel pairing: generation and what happens when supply and use do not align. In both branches, the second topic prevents the first from becoming an isolated solution detached from the surrounding system.

Agroecology brings the food-system branch toward practice, while the climate course stays at a much broader scale. These are connected lenses, not a compulsory sequence of lifestyle changes.
